title: Robust Neural Stimulation Response Modeling Through Meta-Learning and Pretraining
abstract: arXiv:2608.26649v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Objective: Model-based closed-loop neural stimulation holds promise for therapeutic applications ranging from Parkinson's disease to sensory restoration, but deployment has been limited by two obstacles: 1) forecasting models for predicting the consequences of stimulation fail catastrophically on a meaningful fraction of sessions, and 2) per-session calibration requirements are often incompatible with clinical constraints. We address both by demonstrating, for the first time, that meta-learning and pretraining can be applied to neural stimulation response modeling. Methods: Temporal basis function models (TBFMs) forecast state-dependent neural responses to stimulation. We extend TBFMs with cross-session pretraining using a novel architecture and algorithm based on model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML), evaluating them on 40 sessions of optogenetic stimulation in primary sensorimotor cortex of two non-human primates. Results: Meta-learning

translated_title: 通过元学习和预训练实现稳健的神经刺激响应建模
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26649v1 公告类型：新 摘要：目标：基于模型的闭环神经刺激在从帕金森病到感觉恢复等治疗应用中具有前景，但其部署受到两个障碍的限制：1）用于预测刺激后果的预测模型在相当一部分会话中灾难性失败，2）每次会话的校准需求通常与临床约束不兼容。我们通过首次证明元学习和预训练可应用于神经刺激响应建模来解决这两个问题。方法：时间基函数模型（TBFMs）预测状态依赖的神经刺激响应。我们通过一种基于模型无关元学习（MAML）的新架构和算法扩展了TBFMs，并加入跨会话预训练，在两个非人灵长类动物的初级感觉运动皮层中进行了40次光遗传刺激会话的评估。结果：元学习（该部分摘要未完整提供）。
tldr: 本文首次将元学习和预训练应用于神经刺激响应建模，通过扩展时间基函数模型显著提高了跨会话预测的稳健性，减少了对每次会话校准的依赖。
en_tdlr: This paper is the first to apply meta-learning and pretraining to neural stimulation response modeling, enhancing cross-session prediction robustness by extending temporal basis function models and reducing per-session calibration needs.
